articles.body:
The 2026-27 NBA season officially kicked off Tuesday as the Houston Rockets held their media day, before the Dallas Mavericks followed suit Friday.

The other 28 teams in the association joined them Monday, ahead of training camps beginning for most teams.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first media day away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their first impressions?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Quick links:

Trade tracker | Transactions | Offseason buzz

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Top NBA media day headlines

LeBron says he envisioned joining Knicks as free agent | Philly stars ready to 'sacrifice'

Clippers apologize to fans, vow to move past investigation | Ingram (Achilles) out

Stephen Curry on choosing to extend: 'This is home'

OKC says focus is on improving, not beating Spurs

Karl-Anthony Towns wants extension to stay with Knicks

Jokic on next Nuggets deal: 'I'm going to sign next year'

Sept. 28

Pistons eye "better version" of Cunningham

Detroit Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff has held a ton of offseason conversations with All-NBA guard Cade Cunningham about seizing greatness and the necessary steps toward improving after last year's playoff run that stretched to Game 7 of the Eastern Conference semifinals.

Bickerstaff has guaranteed "a better version" Cunningham this season, which could be a scary sight after he averaged 23.9 points, 9.9 assists, 5.5 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 33.9 minutes during 2025-26. But Cunningham also led the East in turnovers per game after finishing with the second most in 2024-25.

"I don't have to challenge Cade and that's why he is who he is," Bickerstaff said. "Because he's pulling. He's not being pushed."

Cunningham showed up in a fresh pair of Nike S.T. Charge "Detroit Tough" sneakers in Pistons colors. He will also receive his own signature Nike shoe, which is expected to debut during the second half of the season.

"I'm thankful to be in these shoes. I'm thankful to have the opportunity to represent my family in this way," Cunningham said. "Represent where I come from, but then to represent the city of Detroit.

"In a city like this, it's a blessing. I'm thankful for it, I don't take it for granted and I'm trying to make the most out of it." -- Eric Woodyard

The Charlotte Hornets are waiving guard Rob Dillingham, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Dillingham was traded from the Chicago Bulls on Saturday for Buddy Hield and cash. The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the move.

Dillingham, 21, appeared in 30 games for the Bulls last season, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists.

articles.headline: Evans, Williams, Greenlaw don't have long-term injuries, 49ers say
articles.description: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said Monday that injuries suffered by Mike Evans, Trent Williams and Dre Greenlaw on Sunday aren't considered long-term issues.
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- The San Francisco 49ers finished Sunday's win over the Arizona Cardinals without receiver Mike Evans (ribs), left tackle Trent Williams (shoulder stinger) and linebacker Dre Greenlaw (quad) but they aren't expecting to miss them for long.

Niners coach Kyle Shanahan provided updates on all three injured players Monday, revealing that none of the issues are expected to be long-term and that Evans, Williams and Greenlaw will be monitored as this week goes on with the possibility of playing against the Denver Broncos on Sunday not yet ruled out.

"Really, all three of these guys are kind of in the same boat," Shanahan said.

The 49ers also plan to open the practice window for second-year defensive end Mykel Williams on Wednesday. The No. 11 overall pick in the 2025 NFL draft has been on the physically unable to perform list because of a torn right anterior cruciate ligament. Since he was on the physically unable to perform list to open training camp, he's eligible to return to practice now but can't play in a game until Week 5.

On Sunday evening, it was Evans' injury that drew most of San Francisco's concern, in part because it was unclear whether it was a rib or oblique ailment. But Shanahan said Monday that Evans is dealing with a rib issue that the Niners will manage this week, similar to how they did with Evans' hip injury last week.

Evans departed the game against Arizona in the second quarter, walking slowly off the field and favoring his right rib cage before eventually going to the locker room on a cart. The Niners ruled out a potential return for him at halftime.

"We'll have to evaluate him throughout the week," Shanahan said. "It shouldn't be long-term and we've got to see how it goes throughout the week."

Trent Williams suffered a stinger in his shoulder and neck area in the third quarter and also went to the locker room on a cart. He soon returned to the sideline but did not reenter the game as Vederian Lowe finished the game at left tackle.

Shanahan said Trent Williams "should be good to go by Thursday's [practice]," noting that the team will keep an eye out for any issues stemming from the stinger.

Greenlaw left the game late, returned for one play then went to the sideline for good with Shanahan saying after the game that they "shut him down." Shanahan said Monday that Greenlaw has a bruised quad but again indicated that Greenlaw will just have to go easy this week, so the bruise heals.

Elsewhere on the injury report, Shanahan said defensive end Nick Bosa (calf) and defensive tackle James Thompson Jr. (ankle) will not play Sunday against the Broncos. Shanahan added that the team is hoping that rookie defensive end Romello Height (broken hand) will return to practice this week after missing Sunday's game against Arizona.

articles.headline: Javier Aguirre turned down four coaching offers until 'Valencia called'
articles.description: Former Mexico coach Javier Aguirre said he turned down four other jobs before accepting the challenge to return to LaLiga with Valencia.
articles.body:
MADRID -- Veteran coach Javier Aguirre said he turned down four other jobs before accepting the challenge to coach struggling Spanish club Valencia, and vowed to regain the fans' support with victories.

Aguirre, taking over his seventh different Spanish club after coaching his native Mexico at the World Cup, was officially presented as Valencia's new manager on Monday.

"I had turned down four other job offers and was happy spending time with my family, but when Valencia CF called, I told my wife we had to come here," the 67-year-old Aguirre said. "She loves football even more than I do, so she was thrilled about it."

Aguirre did not elaborate on the job offers he turned down before agreeing to replace the fired Carlos Corberán.

The 67-year-old Aguirre's third stint as Mexico coach ended with a last-16 loss to England at the World Cup in Estadio Azteca in Mexico City. He previously coached Spanish clubs Osasuna, Atletico Madrid, Real Zaragoza, Espanyol, Leganes and Mallorca.

Aguirre was given a contract until the end of the season, with a club option to extend the deal for an additional year.

Valencia has lost five of its first seven games of the season and is second-to-last in the Spanish league.

Aguirre said he felt welcomed by the fans and sensed a "positive atmosphere" upon arriving at the club, but acknowledged that "it's all about results, and we hope to deliver them as soon as possible."

His first game will be at promoted Racing Santander on Oct. 11.

"People are going to be tired of messages. We're going to play Racing Santander and we're going to go for the win," he said. "The victory is what is needed."

Before Aguirre's arrival, Valencia fans had been protesting against players and team owner Peter Lim, a Singaporean businessperson they say only treats the club as a business.

"The plan is to win, and for the team to have a style and an identity," Aguirre said. "The fans will gradually get on board as the wins start coming."

His hiring completed an early-season reconstruction of Valencia's soccer operations after its poor start in La Liga. When firing Corberán, Valencia also removed chief executive Ron Gourlay and has since appointed Braulio Vázquez as sporting director.

"Beyond his experience, what I liked the most when we started talking was his eagerness to come here," Vázquez said of Aguirre. "We didn't even discuss financial terms. He really conveyed a strong desire to join. I want to thank him and his coaching staff for taking the decision to come to our club during a difficult time."

Valencia hasn't finished higher than ninth in La Liga since coming fourth in 2017-18 and 2018-19. It was ninth last season.

articles.headline: 76ers say 'sacrifice' key to success after offseason additions
articles.description: The 76ers say they are comfortable with making sacrifices for the benefit of the team after adding LeBron James and Jaylen Brown in the offseason.
articles.body:
CAMDEN, N.J. -- With LeBron James, Jaylen Brown, Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey officially coming together as Philadelphia 76ers teammates during the team's annual media day Monday, Brown was asked how the star-studded group would determine the "alpha" among them.

"Next question," Brown, the 2024 NBA Finals MVP acquired in an offseason trade with the Boston Celtics, replied.

Just because Brown chose to sidestep the question doesn't mean the main stars on the league's latest superteam don't know how much interest their every move will generate.

"You got to try to stay even keel," James said. "Understand that the noise is going to be the noise. What happens outside of this building is going to consistently happen and it's going to be doubled and tripled and quadrupled now that I'm here. It just comes with the territory. I understand it."

James, 41, entering an unprecedented 24th season, said the only way to outrun the scrutiny is to outwork it.

"The work that we put in in this building, the work that we put in when we're on the road, watching film, the work that we put in will take care of itself," James said. "Guys will hold each other accountable.

"Everything that's going on out there does not matter. It does not matter at all. It's about the results and the things that happen in this building for us."

To that end, James, Brown, Embiid and Maxey got on the court together for a workout at the Sixers training complex Monday prior to their media day obligations, Philadelphia sources told ESPN, to get a head start on the journey ahead. Even though training camp doesn't open until Tuesday.

"Going into this year, we just want to get as much time as possible with each other on and off the court, try to create those relationships, which we already have," said Embiid, the 2023 league MVP and a member of the Team USA gold medal group at the 2024 Paris Olympics along with James. "And then build from there. Every single day, wins and losses, learn something and keep evolving. Obviously, everyone has the same goal, and we've got to find a way to accomplish it. Day by day, keep getting better."

As the new group figures out the best way to win together, players will assuredly be asked to do things differently than they have in the past.

Maxey, an All-Star in two of the last three seasons and coming off a campaign in which he averaged a career-best 28.3 points per game (No. 5 in the league), said he welcomes the changes.

Which will be a valuable attitude when trying to incorporate Brown, who was No. 4 in the league with 28.7 points per game. Not to mention the NBA's all-time leading scorer in James.

"I think I'm pretty comfortable playing in any type of situation at this point in my career," Maxey said. "I've kind of played under so many different circumstances. ... articles.headline: Injuries might force Ravens to start rookie OG Vega Ioane at C
articles.description: The Ravens may be force to start rookie offensive guard Vega Ioane at center after losing two centers to injury in Sunday's win over the Cowboys.
articles.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- The Baltimore Ravens are unsure who is lining up in front of quarterback Lamar Jackson on Sunday.

Baltimore's top two centers -- starter Jovaughn Gwyn (ankle) and backup Ethan Pocic (knee) -- were injured during the Ravens' dramatic 34-31 win in Rio de Janeiro on Sunday.

"Both look like they'll be a little bit long-term type of things," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Monday.

Asked if Gwyn and Pocic will be placed on injured reserve, Minter replied, "They're both going to be in that range. We'll figure it out here over the next couple days."

Rookie first-round pick Vega Ioane, who is the Ravens' starting right guard, is preparing to play center. Ioane finished Sunday's game at center but lined up there for only 17 of his 2,149 snaps at Penn State.

"We'll figure out the best five guys to put out there for this particular week as we may add a piece or two obviously from losing a couple guys," Minter said.

Baltimore has struggled to replace Tyler Linderbaum, a three-time Pro Bowl center who signed with the Las Vegas Raiders in free agency. The Ravens lost Danny Pinter, the front-runner to take over for Linderbaum, to a season-ending leg injury in August. Now, Baltimore has had two more centers suffer injuries.

So, the Ravens are already on their fourth option at center heading into the fourth game of the season. But the team is confident Jackson can handle any adjustment.

After Pocic was injured Sunday, Jackson took some shotgun snaps from Ioane off to the side. The first one to Jackson had extra zip to it.

When Minter asked Jackson if he wanted to talk to Ioane, Jackson said, "No, I'll make it work."

"To me, Lamar's the ultimate 'make it work' player," Minter said. "He will make it right. That's how he is. That's how great of a player he is. He doesn't let stuff like that bother him. He doesn't make excuses. He is just that type of guy."

The other injury issue on the offensive line is left tackle Ronnie Stanley, who missed his first game of the season. Stanley has been dealing with a toe injury.

"[The missed game] was a good opportunity to allow this to be something that he might not have to deal with just over and over again [and] that it gave it a chance to hopefully get right," Minter said. "I think he'll be a lot closer this week to being able to push back."

Also, wide receiver Zay Flowers is expected to get a bigger workload after being limited to 21 snaps Sunday in his return from a hamstring injury. Flowers still led Baltimore with 85 yards receiving on five catches, including a 27-yarder that set up the winning field goal.

"Now he's coming out of this thing really ready to push to be back in there closer to full time," Minter said.

articles.headline: Victor Wembanyama remembers NBA Finals loss but 'very hopeful' for season
articles.description: Spurs star Victor Wembanyama said on Monday that he still hasn't recovered from the NBA Finals loss to the Knicks. But he also said the team is in a "great spot" heading into this season and "very hopeful."
articles.body:
SAN ANTONIO -- San Antonio Spurs star Victor Wembanyama admitted at media day on Monday that he still hasn't recovered from last season's 4-1 series loss to the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals.

Still, that disappointment hasn't placed a damper on optimism for the upcoming season.

"It evolves with time," Wembanyama said of the emotional toll he's still experiencing. "But I've had a few [nights where it's] hard to find sleep sometimes or hard emotions. But there's just a point where you accept that you have to go through it, and you have to feel all of it. We're going to face these emotions. We're in a great spot. We're very hopeful, very ambitious and ready."

The league's first unanimous winner of the Defensive Player of the Year award, Wembanyama comes off the shortest offseason of his NBA career, which enters Year 4. The Frenchman still found productive ways to prepare for an upcoming season the team believes will be more difficult than 2025-26.

In addition to spending time training with NBA great Hakeem Olajuwon, Wembanyama and several Spurs teammates visited De'Aaron Fox in the Houston area for workout sessions at his in-home court. Wembanyama later hosted teammates in France for training and sightseeing, calling the fellowship "really touching, really emotional."

"Obviously, we have to go through some emotions, and you do some of that alone, but it's better to do it as a team," Wembanyama said. "I took a lot of positive things from everything we did this summer, just being together honestly. It was amazing."

Third-year guard Stephon Castle described the team's visit with Wembanyama in France as galvanizing.

"It brings us together, brings the guys back around each other," Castle said. "There were no coaches there, just players. [We were] able to talk through some things and work on our game together. It's still after a tough loss. It's not like we're just leaving it there. But being able to come together after something like that and make something positive was definitely beneficial for us."

Wembanyama, with teammate Harrison Barnes in tow, also spent time in August training with a professional rugby team in France. Wembanyama called those workouts "really good for the vestibular system" with "new movement patterns and new ways to develop strength."

Of course, Wembanyama isn't the only Spur still carrying scars from the team's first trip to the NBA Finals since 2014. Mitch Johnson, coming off his first full season as the team's head coach, said it's "been nice to have some time to take a deep breath and reflect on everything." Castle pointed out what "will stay with me the longest is just how close we were to winning it. It'll shape our character for really the rest of our lives."

Barnes, meanwhile, called the whole Finals experience "shared heartbreak," while Fox stressed the difficulty San Antonio faces in returning to the NBA's grandest stage.

articles.headline: Sources: Hornets waiving recently acquired Rob Dillingham
articles.description: The Charlotte Hornets are waiving guard Rob Dillingham one day after acquiring the former No. 8 pick, sources told ESPN.
articles.body:
The Charlotte Hornets are waiving former No. 8 pick Rob Dillingham, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday.

The news comes just one day after the Hornets acquired Dillingham from the Chicago Bulls in exchange for Buddy Hield and cash.

Dillingham, 21, will be looking to join his third team in two years after he was traded from Minnesota to Chicago midway through last season and then again from Chicago to Charlotte.

 

The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the deal as well as got Hield's multiyear contract off their books.

It's been a rocky road for Dillingham since the Timberwolves traded two future first round picks to move up in the 2024 draft and select the Kentucky product with the No. 8 pick.

The 6-foot-2 point guard struggled to break into Chris Finch's regular rotation with the Timberwolves and never eclipsed 15 minutes per game for the team in two-plus years.

Dillingham appeared in 30 games for the Bulls and averaged 9.6 points and 2.8 assists while shooting 42.8% from the field.

articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Sept. 28: Jets, Saints grapple with RB injuries

By Michael F. Florio

New York Jets RB Breece Hall is week-to-week after suffering a quad injury on Sunday, per Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter. Rapoport reported that the injury is not as significant as feared.

That leaves Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis active for the Jets. I would anticipate that Allen, who has been the RB2 behind Hall for the last three years, starts and handles the majority of ground work. Both backs have handled limited volume in their careers, but Allen has been the superior runner of the two. He has a 51% success rate.

Davis is a bit of an explosive runner and has been effective as a pass catcher out of the backfield. While he does not have a touch this season, he has caught 75% of targets in his career and averaged 8.7 yards per catch.

Both Jets backs are worth adding in fantasy as this plays itself out in the coming weeks. Allen will be a flex option in a favorable matchup against the Chicago Bears.

Etienne to miss time with hamstring injury

New Orleans Saints head coach Kellen Moore announced Monday that RB Travis Etienne Jr. has a hamstring injury that will force him to miss time. He did not reveal a specific timetable.

That leaves the Saints backfield with Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller. I would expect Kamara to handle the bulk of passing downs, while the two likely split ground work.

Kamara has seen nine carries in each game he has played this season and racked up seven targets in those two. The efficiency is gone as he has averaged just 2.6 yards per touch. Still, volume keeps him in play as a potential flex option moving forward.

Miller is an option for those deep league players. He is the more efficient runner of the two, but we know the Saints are not going to just hand him the job over Kamara. He should see enough carries to be in the flex range in deep leagues. How the goal line work is distributed between the two will be huge for fantasy purposes.

Both are volume dependent flex options, with low floors, in a tough matchup against the Falcons next week.

articles.headline: Lions post 31 points for record-setting third time to start 2026
articles.description: There just aren't many positions in which you can the push the Lions' offense that it can't get out of.
articles.body:
DETROIT -- Dan Campbell could finally let out a big sigh of relief on Sunday evening.

For 60 minutes, the New York Jets -- led by his former defensive coordinator Aaron Glenn -- pushed his Detroit Lions to the limit as they narrowly escaped with a 31-24 victory at home.

Campbell described the win as being "just what the doctor ordered," with star running back Jahmyr Gibbs scoring three touchdowns and the defense securing a pivotal takeaway.

"I'm just proud of that defensive staff. I'm proud of those players over there and as a whole," Campbell said. "That was a good win."

The offense scored exactly 31 points for the third consecutive game this season, marking the first time in franchise history the Lions have scored 30 or more points in each of their first three games, according to ESPN Research.

Lions quarterback Jared Goff called the point total "our lucky number," and Campbell said he has enjoyed the high-scoring affairs so far.

"I'll tell you what, you're coming to our games? You're loving this now. I mean, these are exciting games. These are exciting," Campbell said. "Come down to the wire. Nobody's leaving early. And that was the point. We're not going to let anybody leave early this year."

With Lions legend Barry Sanders in the building as part of the alumni homecoming festivities, Gibbs pulled out his best impression of the Hall of Famer on a 17-yard rushing touchdown to push Detroit ahead 17-7. On the play, Gibbs faked out the multiple Jets defenders after being tossed the ball, then cut along the left side to find the end zone at 10:56 in the third quarter for his fourth TD of the season.

He also surpassed Billy Sims (42) for the second-most rushing touchdowns in Lions franchise history while trailing only Sanders (99) and his 11-yard touchdown reception from Goff with 2:25 remaining in the fourth gave Detroit its final lead.

"Every time he's here, I gotta step up my game a little bit," Gibbs said of Sanders. "So, to be in the same conversation as him is humbling. I'm blessed to be in it. It's somebody I've looked up to for a long time."

Goff ran the offense like a well-oiled machine, completing 25-of-32 passes for 269 yards, two touchdowns and zero interceptions. He has now thrown a touchdown in 26 consecutive games, which is the longest active streak in the NFL and extends his franchise record.

He was nearly perfect against the Jets' blitz on Sunday, going 15-of-16 for 159 yards and two touchdowns. Through three games this season, Goff has four touchdowns and has completed 77% of his passes against the blitz, both his best marks through three games in his career, per ESPN Research.

"I think I've done a good job of being disciplined and not getting frustrated, I guess, with the lack of deep throws," Goff said. "It's not that we're not calling them. It's just that they're playing with so much depth, and it's my job to not get frustrated and stay within myself and take the checkdowns, and I have, and it's been good."

articles.body:
The NBA season is right around the corner as media days concluded on Monday.

The Houston Rockets and Dallas Mavericks were the first two teams to hold media days last week, as they'll travel to China for a preseason doubleheader. The remaining teams went on Monday with plenty of storylines ahead of a new campaign.

LeBron James and Jaylen Brown headlined the new look Philadelphia 76ers. The New York Knicks rang in the season as champions for the first time in over 50 years. New York's opponents in the NBA Finals, the San Antonio Spurs, eye a return to the final stage, while the Oklahoma City Thunder prepared for revenge after losing to San Antonio in the Western Conference finals.

Here are the top scenes from 2026 NBA media day.

Atlanta Hawks

The offseason acquisition of Lu Dort creates a strong group of defenders in Atlanta with Nickeil Alexander-Walker and Dyson Daniels, who posed together.

Boston Celtics

The blockbuster trade that sent Jaylen Brown to the 76ers created a new Celtics duo: Jayson Tatum and Paul George. The two posed together, while Tatum praised his latest teammate.

Brooklyn Nets

If Brooklyn is in need of any bodies, head coach Jordi Fernandez may be the likeliest to come off the bench. 

Charlotte Hornets

A key offseason acquisition, Naz Reid looked right at home in the Hornets uniform.

Chicago Bulls

Energy was high as players arrived for media day, pinpointing what they were looking forward to the most on the day. Two of the Bulls' young stars -- Matas Buzelis and 2026 No. 4 pick Caleb Wilson -- discussed celebrations. 

Cleveland Cavaliers

Cleveland displayed its new look core after acquiring wing Peyton Watson in a scene full of laughs.

Dallas Mavericks

Reigning Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg was center stage in Dallas. Much to his chagrin, he attempted to stop a timer right at one second, while teammate Naji Marshall cut a banana. Flagg also wouldn't confirm nor deny his offseason growth spurt to 6-foot-11.

Denver Nuggets

For the third straight year, a joker card showed up for Nikola Jokic with this one the biggest yet. Also, various Denver players took turns handling the Nuggets' X page, posting throughout the day.

Detroit Pistons

Coming off a second consecutive All-Star season, Cade Cunningham was all smiles posing in his uniform.

Golden State Warriors

Vibes were high in Golden State with Stephen Curry showing off the dance move, and Jimmy Butler III rocking new bling. There was also some friendly banter between Draymond Green and Yaxel Lendeborg, who played for Michigan. Green suited up for the in-state rivals Michigan State.
